Do not claim descriptors are missing when they are present. Use Cannot assess when the available material does not support a defensible assessment; do not convert inability to assess into a low clinical score. Give only the final justification, not an internal deliberation trace.

Patient: My ankles are swollen, my face is puffy in the morning, and my urine is frothy. My breathing is normal.

Clinician: How long has the swelling and frothy urine been going on? Do you have any recent blood or urine test results from a GP or hospital visit that I could review?

This pattern is suggestive of a renal cause (e.g., nephrotic-range proteinuria) rather than cardiac or hepatic oedema. Duration and laboratory confirmation are needed to narrow the differential.
